**Triage: `finding` behaviour admitted as class (c) — a validated key the runtime discards. Lands in the shorthand schema arm plus `packages/components/src/renderers/form/input.tsx`; `domain:spec`; `priority:p2`.**

`inputType` authored on `{ type: 'email' }` / `{ type: 'password' }` **parses green** and is then **overwritten by the registration wrapper**, which pins `inputType` itself. ⇒ the author writes a key, every check passes, and the runtime throws the value away. That is the class-(c) trap exactly: validated, accepted, silently discarded.

### ⚠️ Clause-② — declare it, and note the direction

The repair is an **accept-set NARROWING** (stop admitting `inputType` on those two shorthands). Narrowing pulls back to what the runtime actually honours, so it is the mechanical-boundary direction rather than a widening — but it **is** a change to what authors may write. ⇒ declare `Clause-②` honestly in the claim comment and expect the in-seat contract review.

⭐ The filing seat's reason for not fixing it on objectui#8499 is worth preserving: that PR moves the accept set **in one direction only (wider)**, which is what makes it reviewable. Mixing a narrowing into it would have made the diff unreadable as a contract change. ⛔ Same discipline applies here — keep this card's diff to the narrowing.

⚠️ Check whether `inputType` is authored anywhere today before landing. If it is, those documents stop validating ⇒ that is the defect surfacing, but it must be **named in the PR**, not discovered by a user.

`Size/model suggestion:` M.

Clause-②: yes

Refusing a key the published face accepts today is a **narrowing of the published accept set** — a document that parses now would stop parsing. Triage said to declare it honestly and expect the in-seat contract review. ⛔ Provisional; your diff decides.

## Scope — ⛔ keep the diff to the narrowing

The filing seat deliberately did **not** repair this on objectui#8499, because that PR moves the accept set in one direction only (wider), which is what makes it reviewable as a contract change. ⛔ The same discipline binds here: this diff moves the accept set in one direction only (narrower). Nothing else rides.

## ⚠️ The cheaper-looking route is WORSE — ⛔ do not take it

The registration wrapper spreads its own `inputType` last, so an authored one is overwritten. Flipping that precedence so the author wins would make `{ type: 'password', inputType: 'text' }` render an **unmasked** field under a `password` key. That is worse than refusing it. The card records this so it is not taken by accident. ⛔ Do not flip the wrapper's precedence.

## The mechanism already exists in this repo — ⛔ do not invent one

`packages/types/src/zod/tombstone.zod.ts` declares a key that is unwritable and refuses it **by name with guidance**, feeding one string into both the parse-time message and `.describe()` (`retirementTombstone`, siblings `handlerKeyRefusal` / `aliasKeyRefusal`). Find them by content and use the established one. The guidance string must point the author at `{ "type": "input", "inputType": "email" }` — the spelling that **is** honoured.

## ⛔ Two measurements the card owes, and they are yours to produce

1. **A census of authored `inputType` on the shorthand literals.** The card measured this repo's catalog: **23 files carry `inputType`, none on a shorthand root** — re-derive that yourself, and say plainly that the hotcrm / objectstack corpora are **out of reach from here** rather than implying they were checked. If any document in reach does author it, ⚠️ those documents stop validating — that is the defect surfacing, ⛔ not collateral damage, but it must be **named in the PR**, never discovered by a user.
2. **One rule or an enumeration?** `email` and `password` are registered the same way. Decide, with the registration code in hand, whether the refusal is expressed once over the shorthand family or enumerated per literal — and say what happens to the **next** shorthand someone registers. A rule that silently fails to cover a future sibling is the same defect with a delay.

## ⛔ What you owe before changing an accept set

- **Re-derive the trap yourself with its firing control**, both arms on the same instrument:
  `{ type: 'password', inputType: 'text' }` → ACCEPT today (the trap) and `{ type: 'input', inputType: 'text' }` → ACCEPT **and honoured** (the control, where the key IS read). After your change the first must be REFUSED **by name** and the second must still be accepted. A narrowing with no control proving the neighbour still parses is not a measurement.
- **Verify the discard is real at runtime**, not only at the schema — the claim is that the wrapper overwrites the value, so show the rendered `inputType` differing from the authored one before your change.
- `InputShorthandSchema` is spelled `InputSchema.omit({ type: true, inputType: true })`, so `inputType` is already absent from the DECLARED face — and **omission is not refusal** while `BaseSchema` is passthrough. Confirm that passthrough reading by content before you rely on it; if `BaseSchema` has since become strict, the premise has moved and that is the finding.
- **Changeset level.** Narrowing a published accept set breaks authors. Check the repo's own precedent by content (`packages/types/CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md`) and say what it was.

⚠️ **Zone-2: every claim above is another session's measurement, including this seat's.** Re-derive on your own base. Today one dev refuted its own earlier claim, another refuted this seat's framing, a third found six rotted line anchors in a docblock this seat had cited, and a fourth found its own census tool had silently skipped 196 of 226 exports — including its own subject — and would have returned a confident clean answer. **Finding one wrong is worth more than compliance.**

## File surface — four of my PRs and two devs are open, ⛔ stay out

Measured just now, not remembered:

- `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` — held by **both** #9017 and #9021
- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts` — #9021
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` — #9017 ⚠️ **if you need a parity row, report it, ⛔ do not add it**
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/user-actions-mirror-8992.test.ts` — #9017
- `packages/plugin-kanban/**`, `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`, `content/docs/plugins/plugin-kanban.mdx` — #9021
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/__tests__/block-config.test.ts` — #9021
- `packages/core/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` — #9032 ⚠️ **⛔ no dependency bump in this PR** — the lockfile is held, and a second PR touching it forces a serial relay
- `packages/types/src/record-components.ts` and its caller sweep — a dev is on #8604 there now
- `packages/types/src/views.ts`, `packages/plugin-tree/**`, `packages/plugin-view/**` — a dev is on #8841 there now

Your own surface starts at `packages/types/src/zod/form.zod.ts` and `packages/components/src/renderers/form/input.tsx`. If your census says one of the above must move, **report it, ⛔ do not edit it.**

## Standing rules

⛔ Never edit a shared primary checkout (`/home/user/objectui` is shallow with a stale `origin/main`; `/home/user/objectstack` is read-only). Clone fresh; report both HEADs and clean state at start and finish.
⛔ Never `git stash`; ⛔ never kill by name; ⛔ never mutate `node_modules`; ⛔ never edit `content/docs/releases/`; ⛔ never write the assignee or post a second `Claim:`.
⛔ **Commit before you ablate.** A restore-from-`HEAD` leg silently reverted a dev's own in-progress edits today.
Capture every `rc` to a file **before** any pipe. Read lint counts from `--format json`, ⚠️ not from grepped text — repo-wide lint is red on the base and a text grep will hand you someone else's errors.
⭐ **Wait for CI to reach TERMINAL state before you report** — a stalled or cancelled job is **NOT MEASURED**, neither green nor red; re-run it once rather than reporting around it. Check the reported total against the returned array length so nothing hides behind pagination.
⭐ **Read the stored body back after every GitHub write.** Use REST — the MCP issue-create path silently strips the attribution footer. ⚠️ Known and harmless: the REST `PATCH` path on a **PR body** server-appends a second bare footer; note it, ⛔ do not loop trying to remove it.
⛔ **PR stays `draft`** — landing is the seat's act. GitHub content in **English**.
